A standard, first published in 1983, for how electronic instruments, controllers and computers send performance and control data to each other. It sends instructions such as "play this note" or "turn this knob", not sound.
MIDI/Message — the kinds of messages MIDI sends: MIDI/Note, MIDI/Aftertouch, MIDI/CC, MIDI/Program Change, MIDI/Pitch Bend, MIDI/SysEx and MIDI/Clock.
Logseq/Entity/MIDI/Port — the named connections a device presents to a computer.
MIDI/Q/Which MIDI CC numbers are free for custom mappings?
Pressure on a key or pad after it has gone all the way down, sent as one of two MIDI/Message types.
Polyphonic Key Pressure (A0h–AFh) sends a note number and a pressure value, one stream for each held key.
Channel Pressure (D0h–DFh) sends one pressure value for the whole channel: the greatest pressure among the held keys.
The Launchpad Pro MK3 can send either. Its guide recommends Channel Pressure with Ableton Live (Launchpad/UG/10 Setup/04 Aftertouch Settings).
MPE carries per-note pressure as Channel Pressure by giving each note its own channel.
Control Change — a MIDI/Message (B0h–BFh) that sets one controller to a value. It carries a controller number and a value, both 0–127.

The controller number names the control: 1 is the modulation wheel, 7 channel volume, 64 the sustain pedal, 74 brightness by default. On/off controllers such as 64 read 63 and below as off, 64 and above as on.
Fine values. Controllers 0–31 can each be paired with 32–63 for the fine half of a 0–16,383 range: 0 Bank Select with 32, 1 Modulation with 33.
RPN and NRPN. Controllers 101 and 100 (RPN) or 99 and 98 (NRPN) pick a parameter, and Data Entry, 6 and 38, sets its value. RPN 0 sets the MIDI/Pitch Bend range.
Channel mode messages. 120–127 are reserved: All Sound Off (120), Reset All Controllers (121), Local Control (122), All Notes Off (123), Omni Off and On (124, 125), Mono (126) and Poly (127).
The numbers the spec leaves undefined, and so free for custom mappings, are on MIDI/Q/Which MIDI CC numbers are free for custom mappings?.
In this garden: Microfreak/UG/17 Ext Gear/09 MIDI CC Control, Microfreak/UG/21 Appendix D - CC Values, Launchpad/Custom/1/Arrangement.
The MIDI/Message types that keep devices at one tempo and start and stop them together. They are system real-time messages: they carry no channel and may arrive in the middle of any other message.
Timing Clock (F8h) — sent 24 times per quarter note. The tempo is the spacing between them; the message carries no number.
Start (FAh) plays from the beginning, Stop (FCh) halts, and Continue (FBh) resumes where playback stopped.
Song Position Pointer (F2h), a system common message, tells a follower where to resume, counted in sixteenth notes of six clocks each.

One device sends clock and the others follow. Ableton Live can do either (Ableton/Live/UG/37 Sync with Link Tempo Follower and MIDI/03 Synchronizing via MIDI), and sends clock to the MicroFreak over Microfreak/MIDI/Port/Arturia MicroFreak.
